public_rationale: Google's model card identifies TPU training, and AFP explicitly reports that Gemini 3 was trained without Nvidia technology. Independent launch testing places Gemini 3 Pro ahead of competing models on a broad capability index. Together, these support the claim when read as a statement about training accelerators and overall launch performance.
limitations: The explicit exclusion of Nvidia relies on reputable reporting rather than a fully readable primary confirmation.
The evidence does not establish that every supporting computation used TPUs.
Broad benchmark leadership does not mean winning every test.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Google achieved better results than competitors with Gemini 3 without Nvidia GPUs, using only its own TPUs.

statement.excerpt: But biggest news was buried in the methods: Google got better results than it is competitors without using Nvidia GPUs, relying solely on their own TPUs:

from_speaker: relying solely on their own TPUs
our_interpretation: The methods reference makes model-training accelerators the ordinary hardware scope. This does not assert that Google's entire business uses no Nvidia hardware.
Better results means broad benchmark leadership at launch, consistent with the surrounding phrase 'on most measures'; it does not mean winning every benchmark.
The period covers development of the launch model and its results through November 19. The training start date is unspecified.
Evidence dates for hardware provenance refer to the released model whose provenance is described, not an invented training-completion date.
criteria.support_condition: Technical disclosure and reliable reporting establish TPU-only training without Nvidia GPUs for Gemini 3 Pro, while comparable launch evaluations establish broad performance leadership over competing models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish Nvidia GPU use in the model's training, or comparable launch evaluations show that the claimed broad performance advantage did not exist.

evidence.explanation: AFP retrospectively reports the absence of Nvidia technology in Gemini 3's training. This supplies the explicit exclusion missing from the readable primary disclosure; the event date identifies the launch model, not the later article's publication.

Independent launch testing supports broad comparative leadership. The article reports leadership in five of ten constituent evaluations, so it supports aggregate superiority rather than a clean sweep.
